label: R1
tier_justification: folklore made precise: rustc's const-eval interpreter requires `Scalar::Initialized` components for its immediates, and MiniRust's pointer decoding keeps a provenance just when the bytes are one pointer's fragments at matching positions; CompCert mechanizes a related byte model, but no mechanized iff of this form was found
plain_claim: Let `V` be any set of byte-level values, each of length exactly `n`, and let the representation be one scalar `s` of any width (the scalar's extent may run past the value; `seg` and `place` are truncated). Then the round trip `raise n ∘ lower` through `Scalar s` refines the identity on every value of `V` iff, in every value of `V`, with `bs` the (truncated) segment of the scalar's extent: (a) every byte below `n` outside the scalar's extent is `uninit`; and if `s` is `initialized p rng`: (b) `bs` is all initialized or all uninitialized, (d) if `bs` is all initialized and non-empty, its data lie in `rng`, and (c) unless `bs` is all uninitialized, `bs` is provenance coherent for `p` (integer: no pointer fragment; pointer: no pointer fragment, or one pointer's fragments with one provenance in order from position `0`).

hypotheses.name: hlen : ∀ x, V x → x.length = n
hypotheses.purpose: values have the type's size, so lengths match after raising
hypotheses.witness_class: tight for the `←` direction: `cex_scalar_hlen` (a 1-byte `union` scalar with `V = {[]}`); the `→` direction holds without it (`scalar_conditions_of_roundTrip_refines`)

hypotheses.name: (a) OutsideExtentsUninit, premise of ←
hypotheses.purpose: bytes outside the extent are dropped by lowering
hypotheses.witness_class: tight: a 1-byte integer scalar in a 2-byte value

hypotheses.name: (b) InitUniform, premise of ←
hypotheses.purpose: a partially initialized `initialized` scalar lowers to poison
hypotheses.witness_class: tight: a 2-byte integer scalar with one `uninit` byte

hypotheses.name: (d) RangeIncl, premise of ←
hypotheses.witness_class: tight: a 1-byte scalar with `nonZeroRange` holding `0`

hypotheses.name: (c) ProvCoherent, premise of ←
hypotheses.purpose: an integer scalar drops provenance; a pointer scalar drops mixed provenance
hypotheses.witness_class: tight: pointer fragments under a 2-byte integer scalar; also fragments of two provenances under a 2-byte pointer scalar

non_claims: Not a statement about typed copies at the value's type (which reset padding to `uninit`); it concerns replacing a byte-level move by registers.

"Uniformly initialized" is all-or-nothing, not "fully initialized": an all-`uninit` value round-trips through an `initialized` scalar because `poison` raises to `uninit`; this does not license a `noundef` attribute on that register: `initialized_allUninit_roundTrips_but_noundef_ub` exhibits such a value satisfying all four conditions whose register is `poison` and trips `noundef`. It also does not model rustc's interpreter, which reports an error on reading uninitialized bytes as a scalar, nor LLVM's distinction between poison and undef in memory.

The byte order is MiniRust's; the converse "agreement of every typed read implies `BytesLe`" is false (`typedReads_agree_without_bytesLe`: `ptrFrag 1 7 1` and `bits 1` agree on every typed integer and pointer read at every offset and width).
Nothing about calling conventions, vectors, floats or alignment.
Ranges are arbitrary predicates; nothing is claimed about wrapping intervals specifically.

Real `Scalar::Initialized` layouts in rustc have no trailing padding (the scalar's size equals the layout size); condition (a) concerns the toy's general representations and arises in practice for `ScalarPair` and padded values.

Degenerate edges: `n = 0` (then `V ⊆ {[]}` and (a) is vacuous); `s.size = 0` (then `bs = []` and (b), (d), (c) hold, so the round trip refines iff every byte is `uninit`); `V` empty (both sides hold).
Model–system relation: none proved. This is a statement about the toy model; it neither establishes nor refutes the corresponding claim about rustc, LLVM, Miri or MiniRust.

design_question: Which components of a value may be lowered to two scalar registers without changing its bytes; in particular whether pointer fragments may straddle the two scalars. By R2's condition (c) (derived from `pair_roundTrip_refines_iff`; not proved here as a separate theorem), a non-`union` component whose segment holds a pointer fragment must be a pointer scalar whose segment consists of fragments of one provenance at positions `0`, `1`, … in order. So a pointer whose fragments lie in both segments needs `b` to be `union` (its fragments in `b`'s segment do not start at position `0`), and needs `a` to be `union` as well when it starts at an interior offset of `a`; when it starts at offset `0`, `a` may instead be a pointer scalar whose range admits the data.

label: R16
tier_justification: re-derivation: a constant fill overwrites the lanes a partial write leaves untouched
plain_claim: For every fill byte `fill`, there is a two-byte value `x` such that writing `bits 1` at offset `0` and reading both bytes as an integer is defined, and the same read after a whole-register write of width `2` that puts `fill` in the untouched lane is not at least as defined (`¬ OutLe`). (The first read is defined because `OutLe none _` always holds, so `¬ OutLe` forces it to be `some _`.)
non_claims: Covers whole-register writes with a constant fill on a two-byte register; other widths are not examined.

`¬ OutLe` means "not at least as defined", not "less defined": `OutLe` is a partial order. For every initialized fill byte (`bits b` or a fragment) and every byte list `x`, the whole-register read is not strictly less defined than the partial-write read (`wholeWrite_init_fill_never_strictly_less_defined`); with fill `bits 0` and `x = [bits 7, bits 9]` the two reads are incomparable (`wholeWrite_bits0_incomparable_with_partial`). With fill `uninit` the whole-register read is UB, and for `x = [bits 7, bits 9]` it is strictly less defined than the partial-write read (`wholeWrite_uninit_fill_strictly_less_defined_instance`).
Escape hatches: untouched bytes known to be `uninit`; full-width writes; fills that depend on the old value (a merge, R15) rather than a constant.
